questions.question: In a patient with a EuroSCORE II of 27.36%, multiple comorbidities, and a history of prosthetic valve endocarditis with resolved infection, what clinical factors led to the decision to perform a third transcatheter valve implantation instead of surgical aortic valve replacement?

How does the distinction between active prosthetic valve endocarditis and structural valve deterioration influence the decision-making process for a third valve intervention in a patient with a history of *Enterococcus faecalis* infection?

Which specific pre-procedural multidetector CT (MSCT) measurements were prioritized during the planning phase to ensure the third valve frame would not obstruct coronary blood flow in a previously stented aortic root?

What was the rationale behind implanting the third valve in a high position (supra-annular) relative to the previous Evolut valve leaflets to manage the effective orifice area and complex prostheses geometry?

What distinct pathological mechanisms approximately contributed to the severe restenosis and prosthetic dysfunction observed between the second TAVI procedure in 2022 and the third intervention in 2024?

At the one-year follow-up, which specific hemodynamic parameters and clinical signs demonstrated the long-term durability and functional success of the TAV-in-TAV-in-TAV intervention in this high-risk patient?

If the third valve frame were to fail and lock into the adjacent stents, limiting the ability to perform further repairs, what are the most significant limitations regarding surgical or catheter-based salvage options described in this scenario?
